---
title: "Status Epilepticus Protocol"
format: html
editor: visual
---

## 1. 0--5 min (Immediate Therapy)

a.  Benzodiazepine first line:

-   IV lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg (max 4 mg) or

-   IV diazepam 0.15 mg/kg (max 10 mg) or

-   IM midazolam 0.2 mg/kg (max 10 mg)

Repeat once if seizures persist after 5 min (total ≈ 0.2 mg/kg lorazepam equivalent).

b.  Monitor airway, breathing, hypotension, and respiratory depression

c.  Obtain STAT EEG (call 50061) and activate neurocritical care/epilepsy teams immediately

## 2. 5--30 min (Early Second Line ASM)

*No drug has proven superiority in benzodiazepine refractory CSE*

If seizures continue, choose one IV ASM:

-   Valproate 40 mg/kg over 10 min (max 3000 mg)

-   Levetiracetam 60 mg/kg over 5--10 min (max 4500 mg)

-   Lacosamide 400 mg IV bolus; then 200 mg IV q12 h (max 600 mg/d)

-   Fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg at ≤ 150 mg PE/min (max 1500 mg PE), check free phenytoin level 2 h post load (target 2--3 µg/mL); if below goal, re dose: 0.8 × W kg × (desired -- actual) × 10 mg (round to 250 mg)

-   Phenobarbital load 20 mg/kg in 5 mg/kg increments at \~1 mg/kg/min 1,2

Start continuous video EEG monitoring.

## 3. 30 min (Refractory CSE)

If seizures persist after adequate benzo + second line ASM, you may either:

Repeat a bolus of second-line ASM (levetiracetam, phenytoin/fosphenytoin, valproate, lacosamide, or phenobarbital). OR

Initiate continuous anesthetic infusion:

-   Midazolam bolus 0.2 mg/kg IV (repeat up to 0.4 mg/kg), then infusion 0.1--0.6 mg/kg/h (titrate to EEG burst suppression; max \~2.9 mg/kg/h)

-   propofol infusion (1--5 mg/kg/h)

-   pentobarbital infusion (1--5 mg/kg/h)

-   Consider Ketamine infusion (1--5 mg/kg/h) in super refractory cases.
